transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

I'm here because I've been having a really hard time with my eating lately. What really scares me is that once I start eating—especially when I’m alone in the kitchen—it feels like I’ve just stepped aside. I can’t make myself stop. The whole time it's happening, I’m in my head telling myself, ‘Janet, put it away,’ but I just keep going anyway. It's completely out of my control, and I just don't know how to fix it on my own.

After these episodes where you feel out of control with your eating, do you ever engage in any behaviors to try to compensate, such as forcing yourself to vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never tried to make myself throw up or used laxatives or anything. And I definitely don't exercise excessively. I mostly just... sit there feeling awful about what I just did, but I don't do anything to try and get rid of the food.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly denies compensatory behaviors (purging, excessive exercise), which rules out Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2) and narrows the diagnosis to Binge Eating Disorder (F50.8).
